messages.author: FikusMikus
messages.text:
Right now there's no way to stop letting coalition members with banking perms withdraw over one's personal deposit. The credited balance stays, but if theres not enough in the shared pot, it cannot be withdrawn.

Please add another button besides the "province visibility" one to opt out of the shared pot and keep deposits fully separate, or add a separate place to deposit. If possible, make the numbers private too.

messages.author: Unknown Identity
messages.text:
This one doesnt make sense to me... i am all for members having their own personal accounts, but dont hide them from bankers. Bankers need to to know what members have so they can ensure there is enough in the bank. Otherwise we could be issuing grants and suddenly realize there isn't enough for a personal account withdrawal. 

In a sense this is already in place, members have personal deposit and donate to coalition. The only thing is it isnt hiding the numbers. 

Or am I misunderstanding what this is asking?

messages.author: Cario
messages.text: I think he wants it to not allow bankers to withdraw personal deposits

messages.author: Unknown Identity
messages.text: Ok i can see that. But dont hide the numbers, so we know what we need to keep for them to be able to withdraw.

messages.author: Cario
messages.text: It wouldnt matter, if you literally couldn't withdraw member deposited funds

messages.author: Cario
messages.text: Like, only donations and taxes could be withdrawn by bankers

messages.author: Cario
messages.text: I dont think i agree, because people will quit the game and their stuff will moulder in alliance banks for all eternity, but i think thats what he's suggesting

messages.author: Cario
messages.text: My suggestion is that coalition balance should be separate from member balances

messages.author: Unknown Identity
messages.text: Ooh I hadnt thought of that. <@710359818329915443> If this passes, will there be safeguards in case the member leaves? Like after a month of inactivity it gets donated to the coalition or something?
